# isGridRangeContainedIn

<link-summary>Checks whether one grid range lies entirely within another.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isGridRangeContainedIn() — Checks whether one grid range lies entirely within another. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/sheet</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isGridRangeContainedIn(gridRange: GridRange, containerGridRange: GridRange): boolean;
```

Containment is inclusive: a range contains itself. An absent bound on the outer range means it is open in that direction and so contains anything on that axis, which is how a whole column or a whole sheet is expressed.

This is the check to run before writing into a range a user chose, so that a write cannot spill outside the area the script owns.

## Parameters

| Parameter            | Type        | Description                                                                           |
| :------------------- | :---------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `gridRange`          | `GridRange` | The [`GridRange`](GridRange.md) object that is potentially a subset (child range).    |
| `containerGridRange` | `GridRange` | The [`GridRange`](GridRange.md) object that is potentially a superset (parent range). |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the first range lies inside the second.

## Examples

### Checking containment

```javascript
const inner = { startRowIndex: 1, endRowIndex: 2, startColumnIndex: 1, endColumnIndex: 2 };
const outer = { startRowIndex: 0, endRowIndex: 5, startColumnIndex: 0, endColumnIndex: 5 };

isGridRangeContainedIn(inner, outer); // => true
```
